cards.front: What is the difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
cards.back: A compiler translates the whole source program into object or machine code before it runs, producing an executable. An interpreter translates and executes the program one statement at a time and produces no standalone executable.

keyPoints.text: compiler translates the whole program first
interpreter translates and executes line by line

mcq.correct: A compiler translates the whole source program into object or machine code before it runs, producing an executable. An interpreter translates and executes the program one statement at a time and produces no standalone executable.
distractors: A compiler runs the program directly while an interpreter produces object code
An interpreter translates the whole program first, a compiler works line by line
A compiler only works on high-level languages and an interpreter only on assembly

cards.explanation: The difference is when translation happens: all at once, before execution, or repeatedly, during it.

cards.back: A translator that converts assembly language into machine code. Assembly is a low-level language with essentially a one-to-one correspondence between its mnemonics and the processor's instructions.

keyPoints.text: translates assembly language into machine code

cards.explanation: A compiler works on a high-level language where one statement typically becomes many instructions, so an assembler is not just a compiler for assembly.

cards.front: State one advantage and one disadvantage of compiling rather than interpreting a program.
cards.back: Advantage: the object code is translated once, so it runs faster and can be distributed without the source. Disadvantage: every change needs a full recompile, so the edit-test cycle is slower and platform-specific builds are needed.

keyPoints.text: source code is not needed at run time

cards.explanation: The trade-off is run-time speed against development speed, which is why large systems are compiled and scripts are interpreted.

cards.front: Name the main stages a compiler passes a source program through.
cards.back: Lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, intermediate code generation, optimisation and target code generation.
cards.explanation: Lexical analysis turns characters into tokens, syntax analysis checks they form valid structures, and semantic analysis checks they mean something, such as types matching.

cards.front: What do the linker and the loader each do?
cards.back: The linker combines separately compiled object files and libraries into one executable, resolving references between them. The loader copies that executable into memory so the processor can run it.

keyPoints.text: linker combines object files and libraries
loader places the executable in memory

cards.explanation: Linking is why a program can call a library routine it never contained the source for.
